evidence.source: 李學勤主編,《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
evidence.field: 小 headword and adjacent 少 entry; PDF pp. 76–77, printed pp. 64–65
evidence.text: Directly inspected both source scans. The 小 headword calls 小 pictographic, interprets its marks as tiny dust or sand particles and as an early graph of 沙, and says it extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大; it reports that meaning in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, citing 《粹》1004 for 小雨. It describes later extensions to low status, contempt, and youth, and says the bronze form had become corrupted, prompting Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 account. The adjacent 少 entry describes 小 and 少 as originally one graph used alike in oracle-bone texts and later differentiated. Forms checked against pixels: 小, 少, 沙, 八, 丨, 大, and 《粹》1004. This verifies the author’s account, not the disputed sand interpretation.
evidence.title: 《字源》, 李學勤主編, 2012, PDF pp. 76–77; printed pp. 64–65

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 小: formation, early uses, 少, 沙 and 雀 records
evidence.text: The database presents two analyses for 小’s early marks: abstract dots signifying smallness, attributed to 商承祚 and 于省吾, or an early graph of 沙 depicting fine sand grains, attributed to 馬敍倫. It reports shared early graphic use of 小 and 少, oracle-bone 小雨, time expressions 小食 and 小采, and later bronze examples. It says 小 in 雀 contributes both ‘small bird’ and sound. Its 沙 discussion gives competing readings of early forms, so it does not establish a sound borrowing of 沙 from 小. The cited examples have no absolute dates on this page.

evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—小

evidence.source: Masaki Nohara, “The reconstruction of the word shao (少) in Old Chinese Phonology,” 中国語学 262 (2015), pp. 57–75
evidence.field: Old Chinese relationship between 少 and 小; discussion and reconstruction, especially pp. 57–75
evidence.text: Nohara reviews proposals linking 少 with 小 through phonetic-series connections and reconstructions involving a nasal onset, and counterarguments based on excavated texts and Min dialects. He argues for *st- for 少 and concludes that the evidence he examines does not support a phonetic relationship with 小. This cautions against deriving a sound relationship from shared early spelling or graphic affinity alone; it does not disprove the reported shared-graph account.
evidence.title: 「少」の上古音について／The reconstruction of the word shao (少) in Old Chinese Phonology

gaps: The marks’ original referent remains disputed: sources offer abstract signs of smallness or fine sand grains. The sand analysis does not establish that 沙 was borrowed phonetically using the name of the depicted object.
字源 reports oracle-bone 小雨 and later time and status-related uses, but no inscription facsimile or absolute artifact dates were checked here; the semantic bridges and chronology remain unresolved.

The shared-graph account for 小 and 少 is reported by multiple sources, but the graphic and lexical relationship remains distinct from a demonstrated phonetic relationship. Nohara’s study argues against such a phonetic link on its examined evidence.
CUHK attributes a sound role to 小 in 雀, but a historical sound relationship was not established here. Local reading rows alone do not demonstrate that role.
The official individual Unihan lookup pages for 小, 少 and 雀 were inaccessible in this run; readings are reported only from supplied local rows.
